relationships.subject: suzetrigine
relationships.evidence_quote: Suzetrigine’s novel mechanism involves highly selective inhibition of the Nav1.8 sodium channel isoform, which is predominantly expressed in peripheral nociceptors (Figure 2) [11–15].

relationships.subject: suzetrigine
relationships.evidence_quote: suzetrigine binds specifically to the voltage-sensing domain 2 (VSD2) of the Nav1.8 sodium channel, stabilizing the channel in its closed state through allosteric modulation.

relationships.subject: itraconazole
relationships.evidence_quote: Strong CYP3A inhibitors (e.g., itraconazole) can increase suzetrigine exposure by 4.8-fold

key_findings: Suzetrigine is the first FDA-approved selective Nav1.8 inhibitor, allosterically binding VSD2 with about 31,000-fold selectivity over other sodium channel subtypes including Nav1.7.
Phase 3 trials showed superiority over placebo (SPID48 29.3-48.4) but not over hydrocodone/acetaminophen; strong CYP3A inhibitors raise exposure about 4.8-fold.
